subject: physics
question_text: What is latent heat of fusion?

mark_split.label: The formula and the value for ice

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 11 Very Short Answer Question 7 (printed p.116). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: the latent heat of fusion is the heat required to convert unit mass of a solid into liquid at its melting point with no change of temperature, Q = mL; for ice L = 80 cal g⁻¹ = 3.36 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹ (NCERT Class-11 value).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The latent heat of fusion is the heat
needed to change one kilogram of a
solid into liquid at its melting
point, with no change in temperature.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Unit mass and no change of temperature must both appear.
steps.why: While a solid melts, the supplied heat goes into separating the particles held in its fixed lattice, not into raising their speed, so the thermometer stays fixed at the melting point throughout.
common_mistakes: Leaving out that the temperature stays constant while the melting happens.

recall.must_convey: That it is the heat needed to change unit mass of a solid into liquid at its melting point without a change of temperature.

steps.memory_tip: Latent means hidden: the heat is supplied but the temperature stays the same while melting happens.

steps.label: The formula and the value for ice

lines.text: Q = mL, L in J kg⁻¹

lines: L is the latent heat of fusion of the
substance and m the mass melted.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write Q = mL together with the value for ice.
steps.why: The heat needed is proportional to the mass being melted, so the total heat is the mass multiplied by the heat needed to melt one kilogram.
common_mistakes: Giving the value of L only in cal g⁻¹, without the SI value in J kg⁻¹.

recall.must_convey: That Q = mL and that for ice L = 3.36 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
accept: three point three six into ten to the five

steps.memory_tip: Multiply by the mass melted: Q = mL, and for ice L is 3.36 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.

insider_note: Two marks — the definition carrying unit mass and no change of temperature, then Q = mL with the value for ice, 3.36 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
